title: Can Lower(ed) Expert Opinions Lead to Better Consumer Ratings?: The Case of Michelin Stars
eligible_reason: Michelin star changes occur at restaurant-specific guide-publication dates (aroundyear 2011-2020, 10 distinct years), but no reported specification is a panel TWFE/event study. Method 1 (SCM-DiD, Tables 6, 10, 15, 16, 18, E.1-E.4) regresses a collapsed before/after outcome (one pre and one post observation per restaurant-window, 90- or 60-day windows) for each treated restaurant and its synthetic-control twin (syn_control==1 rows carry weighted_* outcomes) on after_90 plus after_increase and after_decrease, with pair-window FE and restaurant FE and, in most columns, time-varying controls (cumulative reviews, cumulative rating, variance, Google searches). Method 2 is synthetic DiD (Arkhangelsky et al.) estimated per cohort in R and aggregated in a spreadsheet. The treatment is split by direction (increase vs decrease) into two regressors, the comparison unit is a synthetic control, the panel is a two-period pre/post collapse within each window, and the period FE is a window-relative post indicator rather than calendar-time FE. Excluded under the synthetic-control, two-period, and additional-treatment-regressor rules.
design_notes: Package: 8.Replication Code/ with Section2-6 and AppendixB folders; Readme.pdf. Stata files: Section4/Table6.do (lines 28, 30), Table10.do, Section5/.../regression_main.do (Tables E.2-E.4), TableE1_SCM_DiD.do, Section6/Table15.do (rule-based control DiD), Table16.do, Table18.do (NYC replication, areg restaurant FE + aroundyear FE, same after_90/after_increase/after_decrease structure). Data: Section4/Data/SCM_DiD.csv (892 rows = 223 restaurant-windows x {treated, synthetic} x {pre, post}; 189 restaurants; after_increase=1 in 152 rows, after_decrease=1 in 71), Section6/Data/Rule_based_control.csv (572 rows, 235 restaurants, 2 obs each), Section6/Data/NYC_replication.csv (252 rows, 47 restaurants). All data are pre-collapsed pre/post aggregates; no restaurant-by-period panel is shipped. R files implement SynthDiD cohort-by-cohort. Python files produce descriptives and bootstrap SEs.
estimators_reported: scm_did (synthetic control twin + pre/post DiD regression)

specs.exclusion_reason: synthetic-control comparison unit; two-period pre/post collapse; treatment split into after_increase and after_decrease regressors; pair-window FE instead of calendar-time FE
specs.treatment_var: after_90, after_increase, after_decrease (+ ifOneStar ifTwoStar ifThreeStar)
specs.notes: column 2 adds weighted_lg_no_of_reviews weighted_cum_avg_rating weighted_cumvar weighted_google_search_count

specs.exclusion_reason: two-period pre/post collapse; treatment split by direction; window FE (aroundyear) not calendar-time FE

data_access: partial (collapsed pre/post pair-level aggregates derived from TripAdvisor and Michelin data; no raw panel)
screener_notes: Full text unavailable; screened from Readme.pdf and code. The abstract confirms the paper 'applies two synthetic-control-based methods'. Even the rule-based-control robustness (Table 15) is a two-period collapse with direction-specific treatment regressors.
